races.name: Newly Weds Sara & Nigel Irish EBF Fillies Maiden
Griffin Auctioneers Maiden

runners_data.name: Davy Crockett
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained veteran with a solid record on Good ground (5W, 3P from similar-going runs) but naturally wants to race last of all — here he is pushed into a midfield berth on the map simply because there are too many hold-up types for the rear of the field to accommodate them all, which dilutes his chance in a shape likely won up front.

runners_data.name: Nothingbutadream
runners_data.note: Has shown a tendency to fade in the finish across his two runs, both on acceptable ground; held up in style but 0W0P in similar-going efforts and coming off a 99-day absence with an apprentice rider, making this a tough ask in even a modest maiden.

runners_data.name: Onlytheriverknows
runners_data.note: Completely unknown on the clock — no public form to assess and lightly raced flag attached; O'Keeffe is an experienced jockey who will give a fair steer, but the absence of any form data makes this horse impossible to place in any scenario with confidence.

runners_data.name: Solness
runners_data.note: The race's sole front-runner and clear pace-setter; has 11 runs on similar going with five wins, nine placings, and recent evidence of competing at this trip for O'Brien — Slevin takes the ride and will know exactly how to exploit an uncontested lead on Good ground.

runners_data.name: Glittering Gem
runners_data.note: Weld-trained filly with two recent placed efforts on Good turf at shorter trips, suggesting she handles the ground well; her prominent style (mapped P) is perfectly matched to a race Solness will control at moderate pace, and stepping up to 1m4f from 10f is a logical progression.

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Six-year-old who prefers to race from the rear but is displaced onto the midfield map here because the hold-up berths are oversubscribed — the style-fit flag (0.93) signals a meaningful discount; his nine-run record on Good ground shows consistent finishing without reward (0W0P).

runners_data.name: Keep It Together
runners_data.note: A confirmed fader in finishes across his form figures, and his Good-ground record (12/13 in similar going) confirms he rarely threatens; at eight years old and returning just eight days after a run, there is little to encourage.

runners_data.name: Shirzan
runners_data.note: Won impressively on Soft ground over this trip but that win came on clearly softer conditions than today's Good; her Good-ground form (6th and 7th from two relevant starts) is modest, and a 97-day absence adds further uncertainty despite Fahey's low recent strike rate.

runners_data.name: Aiteall
runners_data.note: O'Brien's three-year-old has a single run to reference — 13th on Good ground over 9f — and carries the fades-in-finish warning alongside a redistribution flag, meaning his natural hold-up instinct is compromised by the race shape; the lightest weight in the field offers no meaningful compensatory edge.

runners_data.name: Metallic
runners_data.note: O'Brien debutant with zero public form and a lightly-raced flag; Pietropaolo is a 7lb claimer who will be learning alongside the horse, and without any form anchor this runner is a genuine wildcard whose upside and downside are equally unquantifiable.

races.paceDynamic: Solness is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner maiden over 1m4f on Good ground at Tramore, and with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, he will control tempo from the front at whatever pace suits him and his handler J J Slevin. That lone-leader dynamic — uncontested, able to dictate fractions on a flat track — creates a genuinely sustainable, probably modest gallop that will compress the field and make it hard for hold-up horses to find the gaps they need late. The field holds more true hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate: Davy Crockett, Kaleo Ametsa, and Aiteall are all redistributed to midfield on the map, but their natural instinct is to race at the rear; Solness and Glittering Gem are most likely to genuinely secure a forward position. This race shape strongly favours prominent or front-running profiles — a controlled pace set by Solness means horses racing close to him can pounce without having to make dramatic ground, while true closers will find the fractions too comfortable and the run-in too short to deliver a telling late burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Solness Controls, Nearby Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Solness dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is won by a horse tracking him into the straight.
scenarios.body: Solness leads throughout on his own terms, keeping fractions honest enough that hold-up runners cannot build the necessary momentum from the rear; horses racing prominently just off the pace — particularly Glittering Gem — are ideally placed to challenge inside the final two furlongs.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Solness Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Solness is allowed to steal a meaningful lead and his stamina advantage proves decisive in a slowly-run race that never truly picks up.
scenarios.body: With no pressure from rivals early, Slevin can control the pace so completely that the winner-from-front is never headed; Solness's 11-from-15 record on similar going and three prior placed efforts at this trip underpin the possibility he simply outstays a field lacking a genuine challenger.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race, stringing the field out and creating a genuine end-to-end gallop that opens ground for back-markers.
scenarios.body: This is the scenario that suits Davy Crockett or Shirzan, who need a true test of stamina and legitimate daylight to deliver their best; however, the scenario is less likely given that the redistribution flags reveal that many nominal hold-up horses will not achieve their natural rearward berth, undermining the late-finishing threat.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debut/Lightly Raced Upsets
scenarios.trigger: If one of the unknown quantities — Onlytheriverknows or Metallic — proves significantly better than their bare form suggests and benefits from a clean run in the pack.
scenarios.body: Both are O'Brien or low-profile yard runners with no public form to assess, meaning their ability is genuinely opaque; in a compressed, steadily-run race a well-schooled debutant can slot in and produce a winning effort without having to make extravagant ground.

watchPoints.text: Glittering Gem slots in just off Solness and Coen rides a conservative waiting race — if she tracks the leader into the straight on Good ground she is the most dangerous beneficiary of this pace shape.

Solness's tempo will dictate the entire race; watch whether Slevin allows the gallop to drift very slow, because an overly dawdling pace turns the final furlong into a sprint that could theoretically suit a quick-starting hold-up horse over a lone front-runner.

Davy Crockett and Kaleo Ametsa are both mapped to midfield despite being genuine hold-up horses — if they instinctively drop to the back, they will lose lengths they cannot recover in a steadily-run race and their chances will be materially worse than even their modest form suggests.

Shirzan is the one hold-up horse with a course-and-distance win to her name (on Soft), and if the ground is riding on the better side of Good she may not reproduce that form — worth monitoring for any late market drift that reflects trainer/jockey caution.

Both Onlytheriverknows and Metallic are debutants or near-debutants from yards that occasionally produce unexpected winners first time out — any notable market support for either in the ring before the off should be treated as a live signal worth noting.

races.name: Morris DIY Rated Race

runners_data.name: Maxminelli
runners_data.note: De Bromhead three-year-old who has placed consistently at 10f on Good ground and steps up to 1m4f here for the first time, a trip that could suit given his staying profile; naturally prominent, O'Keeffe booking is positive, and 35 days since last run is manageable.
runners_data.comment: Maxminelli has been a model of consistency in recent starts, finishing second two of his last three outings and third the other, and he has run over today's trip and going before; the concern is that he remains yet to win in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Sunrush
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who will be asked to lead from the outset and faces a direct duel with Mare Crisium; Good-ground form is limited to two runs with no wins or places on that surface, and 72 days off is a query, though the 5lb claim of Sam Coen helps offset his 142lbs burden.
runners_data.comment: Sunrush heads the ratings for this contest and has run over today's going, giving him a clear edge on conditions, but he is winless in his last four starts and a 72-day absence adds a fitness question he must answer.

runners_data.name: Rodeo Blues
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's three-year-old arrives here on the back of back-to-back wins at 10-11f on Good ground, making him one of the best-credentialled horses in the field on raw form; a genuine hold-up type who will be delivered late by Pietropaolo, and this trip extension to 1m4f looks a natural progression for his profile.
runners_data.comment: Rodeo Blues won two of her last six starts and comes here just 16 days after her most recent outing, suggesting she arrives fresh and in form, with experience over today's trip and going working in her favour, though a fifth last time out is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Tanzanite Diamond
runners_data.note: Ran just nine days ago and carries the fresh-run concern into this, but has a decent record at 10-12f on Good ground with a place at the trip; McCullagh takes over and the tongue-tie plus cheekpieces combination is worth noting as headgear angles from McGuinness can sometimes sharpen a horse up.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Tanzanite Diamond at least brings distance and going experience to the table and is fit on a nine-day turnaround, though carrying 140 lb looks a stiff ask and his recent unplaced effort gives little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Love Orchid
runners_data.note: Meade filly whose best form has come at 8f, and this extension to 1m4f is a significant step up in trip; her natural instinct is to race at the rear, but with several other hold-up horses in the field she is likely to find herself further forward than ideal — Nicola Burns' 5lb claim is a small positive amid the trip and position questions.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and drawn from a yard with just one success from 23 runners in the past fortnight, Love Orchid nevertheless carries experience of today's going and our rating of 68 suggests she holds claims — though that cold trainer form is the real concern.

runners_data.name: A Pretty Penny
runners_data.note: Has a win and two places from ten 10f runs on Good ground and the form figures show she is capable on this going; instinctively a hold-up horse by style, she is pushed into a midfield role by the traffic of closers in this field, which means she won't get her preferred berth and the STYLE_FIT tag should temper expectations accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out gives A Pretty Penny a recent placed effort to build on, though she has been out of the first three in four of her last six starts; having run over today's trip and going before, she arrives after a 39-day break on a workable 133 lb.

runners_data.name: Mare Crisium
runners_data.note: Colgan rides the second confirmed front-runner who will battle Sunrush for the early lead; recent form shows two fourth-place finishes at 10-14f on Good going and she has no wins to her name, making it hard to see her sustaining the pace all the way to the line in a 1m4f contest after a contest at the front.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts, Mare Crisium faces a stiff task ranked seventh of eight on our figures, and consecutive fourths represent her best recent efforts in a largely disappointing run of form, making her hard to fancy despite having experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Tickle The Cat
runners_data.note: Has shown a tendency to fade in the finish and the form string of 080 over a short career is uninspiring; a true hold-up horse who is shuffled into a midfield slot by the crowded rear of the field, and with Going concern absent but trip concern over only running in 12f once before, the overall profile is the most speculative in the race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked last on our figures, Tickle The Cat faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's going before and returns after a 52-day break that may have done her good.

races.paceDynamic: Sunrush and Mare Crisium are the two confirmed front-runners in this eight-runner field and will fight for the early lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested pace over this 1m4f trip on Good ground at Tramore. That contested gallop is likely to be honest rather than suicidal, but the pressure between two genuine pace horses means neither will get a completely soft time of it, leaving the race open to a closer who can track the pace from a prominent position and pounce in the straight. Rodeo Blues and Tanzanite Diamond are the two true hold-up horses with the clearest credentials to benefit from the pace being made ahead of them, while Maxminelli is best placed among the prominent types to slot in and travel off the contested tempo. This race shape clearly favours hold-up horses who can sit off the pace as it is genuinely made for them, particularly those with strong Good-ground form at middle distances. The field holds more hold-up horses than the pace map can show at the rear — Love Orchid, A Pretty Penny, and Tickle The Cat are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map, meaning Rodeo Blues and Tanzanite Diamond are most likely to secure the prime late-running positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Hold-Ups Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sunrush and Mare Crisium push each other along and the pace is honest enough to set it up for a closer finishing strongly.
scenarios.body: Sunrush and Mare Crisium burn each other off leaving the back straight, tiring inside the final two furlongs while the field strings out, and a genuine hold-up horse picks up the pieces with a clean run. Rodeo Blues, with two recent wins on Good ground and strong sim-going figures, is the profile that thrives here, while Tanzanite Diamond also has the raw form to deliver late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the contested pace is firm enough to clear the field but not extreme, and a prominent mover sits just off the leaders and outstays them in the straight.
scenarios.body: Maxminelli slots in behind the two front-runners, travels comfortably off the honest gallop, and proves good enough to wear them down when the pace setters find nothing extra in the closing stages. A Pretty Penny, though redistributed from her natural hold-up role, has the 10f form to be involved if she gets a clear passage from midfield.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two pace horses — most likely Sunrush — dictates at a controlled tempo and the field fails to coordinate a challenge, leaving them stranded.
scenarios.body: If Mare Crisium drops away early or is outpaced by Sunrush to the lead, Sunrush could dictate at a measured gallop and have enough in the tank to hold on, exploiting the fact that several hold-up horses are out of position further back. Sam Coen's claim lightens the weight burden and Good ground matches Sunrush's best profile among his limited form figures.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail, Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or the field races erratically, and the redistributed hold-up types lose their position advantage entirely.
scenarios.body: With Love Orchid, A Pretty Penny, and Tickle The Cat all racing out of their natural position in the rear, a muddled or falsely-run race could neutralise the hold-up brigade and see a less fancied prominent type grab an uncontested run through. This is the least structured outcome and depends heavily on tactical confusion rather than merit, making it the lowest-probability shape in the field.

watchPoints.text: Rodeo Blues is arriving on the back of two wins in a row on Good ground at a progressively longer trip and could be significantly ahead of his OR=69 rating — watch whether Pietropaolo can get a clean run from the hold-up position given the congestion of redistributed horses around him.

Sunrush and Mare Crisium will race against each other for the lead from flag to finish — if one of them unexpectedly drops away within the first half mile, the other may get a soft lead that changes the entire race shape and invalidates the contested-pace scenario.

Three horses — Love Orchid, A Pretty Penny, and Tickle The Cat — are all true hold-up types jostling for the same ground at the rear; watch for a bunched, blocked finish on the inside where they may check each other's runs and lose any residual chance they carry.

Tanzanite Diamond ran just nine days ago and carries recency as a potential edge or a fitness concern depending on how that race took out of her; watch the market move on McCullagh's booking as a proxy for stable confidence after such a quick turnaround.

races.name: Strand Inn Dunmore East Handicap

runners_data.name: Miss Australie
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Adrian McGuinness who has shown ability on Good going but whose best form (a win over 12f on Soft) came in very different conditions; 10 days since last run is not a concern but similar-going record of 0 wins from 7 comparable starts is telling, and she is likely to be stuck in a large midfield group with no natural pace to close on.
runners_data.comment: Miss Australie won four starts back but has found little since, finishing fifth last time out after a run of disappointing efforts in between; she has experience over today's distance and going, though 144 lb is a stiff ask for a mare rated 60.

runners_data.name: Stepdance
runners_data.note: The key pace angle in this race — Henry De Bromhead's six-year-old is the only confirmed front runner and should be gifted an unchallenged lead; strong Good-ground profile (12 from 15 sim-going runs, 3W 3P) is a significant asset, though the STYLE_FIT flag notes she is being asked to race with greater positional responsibility here and her 2024 form tailed off (10th, 9th) after earlier wins.
runners_data.comment: Stepdance has won three times in her last five starts, with a victory three starts back sparking that run of form, but she heads here off consecutive below-par efforts and a hefty 144 lb in the weights tests her stamina for a return to winning ways.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Denis Hogan's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type who has placed three times in similar conditions, with a 4th over this exact trip on Good ground recently; wears tongue tie and was placed over 12f-17f on Good, giving him the stamina and going profile for 1m4f, though he will need the pace to collapse late to get competitive.
runners_data.comment: Tassarolo was third two starts back and has run over today's trip and going, while his rating of 63 ranks him third in the field and he returns quickly on eight days' rest — the main concern is a trainer in poor recent form, firing at just 4%.

runners_data.name: Mullacurry Maid
runners_data.note: Donal Kinsella runner who is a natural hold-up horse but cannot find her usual deep position in this field — the redistribution note reflects she will race closer than ideal; the fades-in-finish flag combined with a weak similar-going record (0W 0P from 2 runs) and 37 days off since her last start make this a difficult profile to be positive about.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts with finishes that rarely flatter, Mullacurry Maid carries 140 lb off an official mark of 56 and is ranked last on our figures, though she has run over today's going before and returns after a 37-day break.

runners_data.name: Preparations
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's five-year-old is authentically a rear-of-field horse being squeezed into midfield by the sheer number of hold-up types in this race; most encouraging form came over 10f on Good when finishing 4th, and trainer T14 strike rate of 3/30 shows some current yard activity, but a 26-day break and the out-of-role positioning tempers any optimism.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Preparations nevertheless appeals as the one to beat here off a weight of 140 lb, with experience of today's distance and going working in her favour and our rating identifying her as clearly the best horse in the field.

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Andrew McNamara's seven-year-old has the most consistent placed form in the field — five runs with finishes of 2nd, 2nd, 4th, 4th and 2nd on Good and similar ground over staying trips — and though forced by field congestion to race in midfield rather than at the back, he has the raw form to be competitive if any scenario other than a perfectly controlled Stepdance lead materialises.

runners_data.name: Go Flo Jo
runners_data.note: P G Fahey's four-year-old is returning from a 267-day absence — easily the longest layoff in the field — and is flagged as a fader in the finish; the hold-up style and weak finishing pattern make a first-time-out run over 1m4f on Good ground an uninviting profile, especially compressed into midfield out of her natural position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and returning after a 267-day absence, Go Flo Jo is hard to fancy at the foot of our rankings, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her 134 lb burden is at least a known quantity.

runners_data.name: Spinning Web
runners_data.note: Margaret Mullins' six-year-old is the only other horse with a prominent racing style and represents the most logical companion to Stepdance in the early stages; wears a hood, and the 69-day absence is worth noting, but if she can track the leader into the straight on her favoured Good ground she has the profile to be involved at the business end.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked eighth of ten on our figures, Spinning Web has run over today's trip and going before but has been largely out of the picture recently, and 69 days off the track adds another question mark against him here.

runners_data.name: Limestone Red
runners_data.note: Tracey Collins' six-year-old wears a hood and is a hold-up type whose best form has come on contrasting surfaces — wins on Soft and Standard; genuine Good-ground form is limited (5 from 15 sim-going, 0W 1P) and 31 days since last run is neutral, while the redistribution into midfield means he cannot use his natural waiting tactics freely.
runners_data.comment: Limestone Red ran a cracker last time out, finishing second on his most recent outing, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; carrying 132 lb is the chief concern for a gelding our rating marks as the second-best in this field.

runners_data.name: Nathema
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's three-year-old carries a 22-day turnaround into this race wearing a hood, and is flagged as a horse that fades late; form figures of 8-8-4-8 on Good and Heavy going show consistency in one direction — away from the frame — and the youngest horse in the field at 3 faces a stiff ask against experienced handicappers over 1m4f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a pair of eighth-place finishes either side of a fourth two runs back, Nathema faces a stiff task at 132 lb, though she has run over today's trip before and a rating of 60 gives her a slim foothold in a field of ten.

runners_data.name: Duleek Street
runners_data.note: John McConnell's eight-year-old is returning from a 377-day absence — by far the most significant absence risk in the race — wearing tongue tie; the hold-up style suits a horse who needs to find fitness gradually, but one year off in an 11-runner field where true rear positions are congested and pace is likely to be steady makes this a very speculative reappearance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after 377 days off the track, Duleek Street's experience over today's trip and going gives him a foothold here, and a rating of 61 suggests more ability than his official mark of 44 implies — though his recent string of seventh, seventh, ninth and eighth places makes faith a stretch.

races.paceDynamic: Stepdance is the sole confirmed front runner in this 11-runner 1m4f handicap and, with no other genuine pace horses likely to push from the front, she should be allowed to dictate at a comfortable, sustainable tempo on Good ground at Tramore. Spinning Web is the only other horse with a prominent tendency and is capable of tracking Stepdance, but the remainder of the field are hold-up or midfield types — many of them redistributed on the map because the sheer volume of hold-up horses exceeds the rear positions available. The field holds significantly more hold-up types than can all settle at the back; Preparations, Metamorpheus, Mullacurry Maid, Go Flo Jo, Limestone Red and Duleek Street are genuine hold-up horses compressed into the midfield grouping because there simply is not enough room behind, meaning several will be forced to race closer to the pace than they prefer. A single, unchallenged pace-setter on a flat Good track over 1m4f creates a controlled tempo that historically rewards horses who can travel prominently and quicken from a handy position — the tactical verdict is that prominent racers who can track Stepdance and pounce in the straight hold the strongest positional advantage, while true deep closers face the task of making up ground against a horse who has had things entirely her own way.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stepdance Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Stepdance is allowed to dictate a comfortable solo lead throughout with Spinning Web as the only tracker.
scenarios.body: Stepdance sets a measured pace with Spinning Web in her slipstream and neither is pressured through the first mile, allowing both to conserve energy before the straight; horses prominent enough to sit within two lengths of the leader going to the home turn are best placed to pounce as the tempo increases.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pick Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough in the first half that midfield horses are able to close the gap on the home turn without burning energy.
scenarios.body: A sedate early tempo paradoxically compresses the field as the home turn arrives, allowing a midfield stalker travelling well to swoop past a tiring leader inside the final furlong; horses who handle Good ground and have strong finishing form in similar flat races benefit most.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse In Straight
scenarios.trigger: If Stepdance, having gone too freely early, stops quickly in the final two furlongs and hands the initiative to a hold-up horse who times a late run.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting in the rear of the midfield group who has been undisturbed early on finds space opening up as the leaders empty in the final furlong; true hold-up horses who have not been forced to race too prominently against their nature are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Spinning Web or another horse pushes forward to challenge Stepdance from the half-mile mark, turning it into a two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: A genuine battle for supremacy between two prominent horses burns each other out and opens the door for a finishing run from a horse sitting in third or fourth, just off the pace; this scenario is the least likely given the scarcity of confirmed pace horses and the controlled nature this race is expected to take.

watchPoints.text: Stepdance (Darragh O'Keeffe) controls the entire shape of this race — if she crosses cleanly and settles at the front unchallenged, the rest of the field is at her mercy and any horse that fails to track her promptly within the first furlong will be giving ground they cannot get back on a flat Good track.

Spinning Web (Nicola Burns, 5) is the only horse positioned to track Stepdance and could exert unexpected pressure if she travels well fresh after 69 days off — watch the gap between them at the half-mile marker as a key indicator of whether the race unfolds as a controlled or contested lead.

Metamorpheus (Conor Stone-Walsh, 3) has strong recent placed form over staying trips on Good ground and is the most consistent hold-up horse in the race — watch whether he can thread through the large midfield cluster as the home turn is negotiated, as congestion at that point could cost him several lengths at a critical stage.

Duleek Street (Siobhan Rutledge) returns after 377 days and Go Flo Jo (Jessica O'Gorman, 7) after 267 days — both hold-up types racing out of their natural position in an already compressed rear group; monitor their early positioning as any erratic or unbalanced behaviour from either could disrupt the runners immediately around them.

The sheer number of genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield — Preparations, Limestone Red, Mullacurry Maid, Go Flo Jo and Duleek Street all redistributed — creates a risk of significant traffic problems on the home turn; jockeys on Tassarolo and Miss Australie will need to be proactive in finding a clear passage if they are to have any realistic chance.

races.name: Perennial Freight Handicap

runners_data.name: Daboya
runners_data.note: Won over 12f and 13f on Good going in recent starts, giving him strong course-and-distance claims; front-runner who is mapped prominently here, and while the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence slightly, his is the natural lead role and he faces no pace rival — blinkered, five-year-old in form.
runners_data.comment: Daboya won two of her last six starts, including back-to-back victories two and three starts back, and has experience of today's distance and going; the main concern is her eighth last time out, coming just three days ago.

runners_data.name: Marmeladova
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and placed over 12f recently, so the step to 1m4f on today's ground is well within range; natural hold-up horse for Robbie Colgan who will seek to travel into the race off a modest pace set by Daboya, and the trainer's recent 1/6 strike rate in 14 days suggests the yard is firing.
runners_data.comment: Marmeladova ran out a winner two starts back and has experience over today's trip and going, with our rating nudging above her official mark to underline her claims; the risk is that unplaced effort last time out, just six days ago.

runners_data.name: Merlin The Wizard
runners_data.note: Two wins at 10f and 12f on Good ground suggest he handles conditions well enough, though the apprentice booking (Reese Holohan 7lb claimer) adds a navigational unknown in a compact field; genuine hold-up type who needs a clear run in the straight — trip looks fine, 16 days' freshness is not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Merlin The Wizard landed back-to-back wins three and four starts back and returns here on a quick turnaround of just 16 days, with experience of both today's trip and going working in his favour; the risk is that his last two outings have brought a ninth and a sixth.

runners_data.name: Expound
runners_data.note: Lengthy absence of 93 days is the headline worry, and the tongue-strap is worn for the first time in this context; showed form at 12f on Good, and Denis Hogan's 1/27 recent trainer strike rate is a cold-yard flag — likely to race prominently alongside Daboya but stamina question after a long break.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 93 days off for a trainer in lean form, Expound faces questions, but he has run over today's trip and going before and our rating of 85 just edges him to the head of the rankings.

runners_data.name: Churchwarden
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead's runner arrives just two days after a run, which warrants monitoring for fitness management; won over 12f on Good and placed over 16f, so the distance is squarely in his wheelhouse — a true hold-up horse that the map redistributes to midfield because the rear is oversubscribed, meaning Gary Carroll will have to be creative about finding space.
runners_data.comment: Churchwarden returns just two days after his last outing, and while he did win last time out, four of his five recent starts have yielded unplaced or mid-field finishes, leaving him hard to fancy ranked sixth of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Rakki
runners_data.note: Won Mullins-trained, which always carries weight, but the form string shows a 2/20f on Heavy and a 5/16f on Good as highlights — genuinely a stayer who has been campaigned at longer trips than today's 1m4f; another natural come-from-behind type that the field's configuration pushes forward on the map, and the step down in trip is a question.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with two unplaced efforts preceding a fifth last time out, Rakki is hard to fancy from seventh in the ratings here, though a lively yard (13 from 40 in the last fortnight) and experience over today's trip offer slim encouragement.

runners_data.name: Berto Ramirez
runners_data.note: Won over 18f on Good and placed over 17f, so today's 1m4f is notably shorter than his optimal range; Andrew McNamara's 0/10 14-day trainer stat is a cold flag, and Jamie Powell inherits a horse that is a true hold-up type running in a race with four others seeking the same deep position — trip and traffic risks combine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Berto Ramirez does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and he was out just 14 days ago; however, despite a light weight of 132 lb, a rating of 77 ranked fifth of seven makes progress hard to envisage.

races.paceDynamic: Daboya is the lone confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 1m4f contest and, with no genuine rival to pressure him from the front, Sam Coen's mount should be able to dictate a measured, controlled gallop on Good ground around Tramore. Expound has shown prominent tendencies and may attempt to sit close, but with no other natural leader in the field the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching, creating a race run at a pace that suits those with stamina over pure finishing speed. Marmeladova, Merlin The Wizard, Churchwarden, Rakki and Berto Ramirez are all natural hold-up types, but the field holds more come-from-behind horses than the track map can accommodate at the rear — Churchwarden, Rakki and Berto Ramirez are redistributed to midfield on the map, yet in reality all three will be seeking to settle deep, creating a congested back half of the field chasing one controlled pace-setter. This race shape strongly favours the prominent-to-midfield stalker profile — a horse that can sit just behind Daboya, track a modest gallop, and quicken from a few lengths off the pace in the straight, rather than a pure closer forced wide or late from a deep hold-up position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daboya Dictates, Stalker Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and one prominent or early-midfield horse tracks him into the straight with cover.
scenarios.body: Daboya controls fractions from the front without pressure, setting a tempo that rewards horses travelling well just off the pace rather than those held up deep in the pack; the winner emerges from the chasing group with a decisive move two furlongs out.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Daboya Stays On To Win
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely modest and Daboya, conserving energy throughout, finds enough in the tank to repel all challengers up the straight.
scenarios.body: A truly sedate gallop means the hold-up horses fail to generate any meaningful late momentum, leaving Daboya — who has won over this trip on Good ground — to extend his advantage or simply not be caught.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens mid-race and the true hold-up runners, despite being crowded at the rear, find a clear passage up the straight.
scenarios.body: One of the deeper-seated horses — most likely Churchwarden, who has form in demanding stamina tests, or Berto Ramirez — gets a clear run and picks off tiring front-rankers; this shape requires the redistributed hold-up types to actually find room and run their own race, which is the constraint.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Daboya fails to stride on or is taken on early, causing the race to become tactical and fragmented with no fluid front-runner.
scenarios.body: The field concertinas, creating a messy finish where positional advantage at the two-furlong pole becomes decisive; this scenario is genuinely unlikely given Daboya's clear supremacy at the head of affairs.

watchPoints.text: Churchwarden and Rakki are both natural hold-up horses who will compete for the same deep position — watch for traffic congestion in the home straight if they are forced wide or blocked behind the compact pack.

Expound's 93-day layoff combined with the tongue-strap first-time use means his fitness and early manageability under Daniel King are genuine unknowns — if he contests the lead with Daboya the pace shape changes entirely.

Berto Ramirez is entered over a trip shorter than his winning range; if Jamie Powell pushes him forward to avoid traffic he races out of character, and if he waits he may find the race over before he can produce his run.
Daboya runs only three days after his last start — monitor in the parade ring for any sign of staleness before assuming he will replicate his recent front-running form at this tight turnaround.

races.name: Brennan's Pharmacy Handicap

runners_data.name: Delta
runners_data.note: Top-rated at OR 93 carrying top weight, ridden by J J Slevin for the in-form Joseph P. O'Brien stable; confirmed front-runner with a win on Good ground and solid similar-going record (7/9 runs), though the step up to 2m from recent 14-16f starts is a stamina question worth noting; has tongue tie fitted.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and a winner five starts back, Delta has run over today's trip and going and arrives here on a retrieval mission off 37 days; his rating of 95 tops the field and he looks the one to beat, even if a recent unplaced run invites mild caution.

runners_data.name: Filey Bay
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins' 10-year-old has solid experience over 16-17f on Good and a recent win at this trip type; Simon Torrens takes the ride and prominent style suits a fast-run race where he can stalk the leaders without being caught up in early front-running battles; sim-going record of 11/15 with three wins is respectable.
runners_data.comment: Filey Bay won on his fourth start back and arrives here fit on 19 days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour; the concern is that he has been unplaced in two of his last four outings, including last time.

runners_data.name: Clear Quartz
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse whose best recent form has come over shorter trips (placed at 9f and 11f) and on Soft or Heavier ground; the step back to 2m on Good is a concern, and the 7lb claim from Joseph Harnett may help, but sim-going record of only 4/15 is a red flag for today's conditions.
runners_data.comment: Clear Quartz has been placed twice in recent starts, landing second three starts back and third five starts back, and he returns fit on 19 days' rest with experience of today's distance and going; the risk is a winless run in recent starts that may give his rivals a fitness edge.

runners_data.name: Plontier
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 at OR 83, Reese Holohan claims 7lb; placed at 12f on Good going and has recent course experience over 17f, though finishing positions have been modest — the tongue-and-pin headgear combination suggests connections are trying to sharpen him up, and he is best watched over this stamina-testing trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Plontier nonetheless showed his quality with a second two runs back, and he returns fit on 19 days' rest with experience of today's distance and going in his favour, though 137 lb is the obvious query.

runners_data.name: Spasiba
runners_data.note: W P Mullins sends out this 7-year-old with Ben Coen aboard after a remarkable 587-day absence; won over 16f on Good ground previously and has multiple placed efforts at staying trips, so the ability is there — the giant question is fitness off such a long layoff, which makes him high-risk but high-reward if Mullins has him spot-on.
runners_data.comment: Spasiba carries a hefty 137 lb yet our rating of 91 ranks him second in this field, and his trainer is in red-hot form at 33% over the past fortnight; a third three starts back underlines he can threaten at this level, though 587 days off the track is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Dream On Baby
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with a win 16f on Good just 2 days ago — the very quick turnaround is a significant concern for stamina over 2m and could see him fade badly late; Robbie Colgan takes the ride for Emmet Mullins, and the horse is likely to press Delta early before finding this trip stretching him.

runners_data.name: Zoffman
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides this hold-up type for Noel Meade, whose stable has had only 1 winner from 23 runners in the last 14 days; Zoffman's sim-going record is poor (12/15) and his recent form string of 70-680 gives little cause for optimism, though he has previous experience over marathon trips including 22f.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and facing a 64-day layoff, Zoffman has experience over today's distance and going but a struggling yard sending out just one winner from 23 in the past fortnight makes improvement hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Way Down South
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse in nature whose instinct is to race from the rear; with front-runners dominating this field's early positions, he is unlikely to find clear racing room at the back, and Nicola Burns (5lb claim) will need to be patient — the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence in him finding his natural rhythm here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Way Down South faces a stiff ask here, though he has experience of today's going and returns on a fresh enough 15-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: Flagged as a horse who fades in the finish, which is deeply concerning in a stamina-testing 2m race on Good ground; Julian Pietropaolo claims 7lb but the OR of just 63 and a sim-going record of 14/15 without strong finishes makes her likely to set pace early before weakening into the straight, acting as a pacesetter rather than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Miss Gitana makes little appeal, though a third last time out at least offers a crumb of encouragement and she has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Delta, Dream On Baby, and Miss Gitana are all confirmed front-runners in a nine-runner field over 2m at Tramore, guaranteeing a strong early gallop that will expose any stamina limitations and make this a genuine test of staying power. Delta (OR 93, top weight) is the most likely to actually dictate from the front given class and recent course evidence, while Dream On Baby (only 2 days since last run) and Miss Gitana (flagged as a fader) are unlikely to sustain their challenge into the closing stages. This fast-run shape over two miles on Good ground strongly favours horses who can sit off a pressured pace and stay on powerfully in the straight — specifically prominent-to-midfield types who conserve energy early and pick off tiring leaders. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position; Delta is best-placed to lead, with Dream On Baby likely pushed wider and Miss Gitana surrendering position under pressure.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hot Pace, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Delta sets a genuine front-running gallop with Dream On Baby and Miss Gitana pressing early, burning off the pace-setters by the final turn.
scenarios.body: The strong early tempo will string the field out and leave tiring leaders vulnerable in the straight, rewarding horses with proven stamina who track the pace without over-committing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Delta Dictates, Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Delta secures an uncontested or lightly-contested lead and is allowed to control fractions from the front.
scenarios.body: With Joseph P. O'Brien's stable in form and Delta showing a win over 12f on Good, the combination of class advantage and front-running control could see him hold on over this longer trip if the pace remains moderate.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final half-mile and a late-running type weaves through weakening horses.
scenarios.body: Clear Quartz has shown ability to finish strongly and Plontier has placed over this trip before; either could emerge if the field concertinas in the straight.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Implodes, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Dream On Baby or Miss Gitana cause early scrimmaging that disrupts rhythm and produces an unusually messy race shape.
scenarios.body: A fractured pace scenario could give Spasiba — returning after 587 days but trained by W P Mullins with a proven win over 16f on Good — a route into contention from a prominent position.

watchPoints.text: Dream On Baby ran just 2 days ago and is confirmed front-runner — watch for early signs of fatigue from the 1m6f pole onwards as the fast pace bites; a sudden capitulation would open the race for hold-up horses.
Spasiba returns after 587 days and W P Mullins has form freshening horses; if he travels suspiciously well in the early stages under Ben Coen, he becomes a live player despite the huge absence.

Miss Gitana is flagged as a fader and carries the lowest OR in the field at 63 — if she leads aggressively from the start alongside Delta, monitor whether she increases the gallop to unsustainable levels, which could compromise all three front-runners.

Filey Bay's rider Simon Torrens will need to judge the pace carefully — if Filey Bay gets caught too close to a suicidal early gallop for a 10-year-old, his finishing effort may be blunted; watch his position approaching the final turn.

Clear Quartz has a poor sim-going record on Good (4/15) but placed most recently over a much shorter 9f trip — if he settles unusually well from the hold-up position and the pace is truly strong, a bold staying-on run into the places is possible without being a headline bet.

races.name: Dan Cowman Memorial Handicap

runners_data.name: God Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator for Denis Hogan who arrives in decent form (2nd last time) on ideal good ground; 9 days fresh, tongue tie and cheekpieces worn, but needs more pace than Gallo Dell Cielo is likely to generate over this 2m trip.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out and yet to win in his last six starts, God Of Thunder at least brings a rating of 66 to the table — top of these 13 — and returns quickly on 9 days' rest having run over today's distance and going before, though a trainer striking at just 4% is a concern.

runners_data.name: Vervain
runners_data.note: Placed in two of last four on good ground and steps up in trip for David Kelly; hold-up style means the steady pace will be a disadvantage, though the 7lb claim from Jimmy Dalton offers some compensation on a mark of 56.
runners_data.comment: Vervain has been winless in her last five starts but shows consistent placing potential, finishing second last time out after two fourth-place efforts; she has run over today's going before and returns on a quick turnaround, though her rating of 55 positions her mid-pack in this field.

runners_data.name: Fine Print
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for McConnell who was second on his most recent start; has strong form at marathon trips and on good ground, and the 5lb claim from Sam Coen is an asset, but still needs the pace to be stronger than this race is likely to provide.
runners_data.comment: Fine Print has run over today's trip and going, and a second two starts back keeps him in the mix, but he's winless in his last five starts and a seventh last time out — just six days ago — leaves fitness less of a concern than his ability to find a way past rivals from a midfield draw.

runners_data.name: Bynx
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by profile — a winner at 16f on good ground for Martin Hassett — who will be forced closer to midfield than his natural rear position given how many closers populate this field; Ben Coen's experience is a plus but the compressed position is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Bynx won last time out to arrive here in form, and she has run over today's trip and going before, but a weight of 138 lb looks a stiff ask and her two prior starts saw finishes of sixth and eighth, leaving her profile mixed heading in.

runners_data.name: Maxwell Smart
runners_data.note: Placed three times on good ground over similar trips and handles this distance well, but his natural instinct to race from off the pace is undermined here — the crowded hold-up division means he'll sit closer than ideal with a 7lb claimer aboard.

runners_data.name: Bhean Saibhre
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a placed record at this trip and course style for Aidan Howard; 25 days since last run but has shown consistent form at 2m on good ground and is one of the few whose natural front-rank style fits what this race shape rewards.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts but has placed three times in that sequence, showing consistent mid-division form; she has run over today's going before and arrives fresh enough on 25 days' rest, though carrying 136 lb may test her chances of converting that consistency.

runners_data.name: Gallo Dell Cielo
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who has won twice on Flat surfaces and is uncontested in the lead role here; the 185-day absence is a significant concern on a mark of 50, and all his wins have come on standard surfaces rather than turf — the going switch and layoff are genuine flags despite the prime tactical position.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back wins two and three starts back give Gallo Dell Cielo a compelling recent profile, and he has experience of both today's trip and going; the concern is a fifth last time out and a 185-day absence that leaves fitness on trust.

runners_data.name: Kings Gesture
runners_data.note: Poor recent record including a string of zeros, and specifically tagged as fading in the finish; genuinely a hold-up type by history but mapped to midfield due to the crowded rear — the combination of out-of-role placement and a worrying form line makes this a very difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Kings Gesture carries a weight of 136 lb on a mark of 50, yet our rating of 63 suggests he is meaningfully ahead of his official assessment, making him a serious threat if that gap translates to the track; the chief concern is a winless run of five starts in recent form.

runners_data.name: Fire Coral
runners_data.note: Course specialist on good ground with two wins and four places at this track over marathon trips for Stuart Curling; a hold-up horse by nature who will find himself closer to the pace than he'd like, though his familiarity with Tramore's unique layout could help him navigate a prominent midfield position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Fire Coral nevertheless steps up in our assessment to 54 against an official mark of 46, hinting at latent ability; she has run over today's going before, but her recent record of two unplaced efforts in her last three makes a bold showing hard to confidently foresee.

runners_data.name: Highway Sixty One
runners_data.note: Prominent-type for L Young whose best form comes at 12f on good ground; stepping up in trip to 2m here and that stamina query is real, but Gary Carroll is an experienced jockey who will allow him to travel comfortably in the lead group where the race shape places horses like him well.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of thirteen on our figures, Highway Sixty One is hard to fancy at face value, though a runner-up finish two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement and he has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Synchronize
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse placed twice on good ground for J Morrison who arrives 39 days fresh; naturally suited to a stronger pace test than this race is likely to produce, and the redistribution into midfield from his true rear position only compounds the tactical mismatch.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked well down the field on our figures, Synchronize faces a stiff task here, though he has run over today's trip and going before and the second two starts back at least shows he can hit the frame.

runners_data.name: Lariat
runners_data.note: Veteran of 10 seasons who stays well and handles good ground, with a recent second at 16f; prominent racer by inclination which suits this shape, though Robbie Colgan will need to judge the pace carefully on a horse whose form is intermittent at best.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pair of sevenths and a sixth before finishing second last time out, Lariat arrives 22 days fresh but is rated 12th of 13 on our figures, making him a tough proposition to fancy despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: Top weight on OR 60 and flagged as prone to fading in the finish — a concerning combination in a 2m race; hold-up style is his default but the finish-fade profile on a sound surface suggests stamina runs out before the line, and the trainer has no recent winners to boost confidence.
runners_data.comment: Stone Rulya has run over today's trip and going, arrives here on a reasonable 23-day break, and a rating of 62 puts him competitive among these thirteen; the concern is that he is winless in his last five starts, with a fourth his best recent effort.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: A horse with three consecutive zeros and a finish-fade flag, making this a very guarded prospect; his hold-up profile places him in midfield rather than his natural rear position, and the complete absence of a jockey listed in the data is an additional unknown that cannot be ignored.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Crypto Crash faces a stiff task, though he has run over today's going before and returns on a quick turnaround of just 12 days, suggesting connections believe he is in decent enough order.

races.paceDynamic: Gallo Dell Cielo is the one confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner field over 2m at Tramore and, with no rival likely to seriously contest early leadership, is set to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on good ground. Bhean Saibhre, Highway Sixty One, and Lariat are prominent-types who will likely sit just off the pace, creating a compact lead group but no genuine pressure on Gallo Dell Cielo's fractions. With the pace modest and the race run at an even tempo, horses that can travel prominently and produce a sustained gallop through the final half-mile will be best positioned — pure hold-up horses who need a truly run race to generate momentum will find this shape insufficient. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Bynx, Maxwell Smart, Kings Gesture, Fire Coral, Synchronize, and Crypto Crash are genuine hold-up horses who are unlikely to secure their natural position and will be closer to midfield than ideal — Bhean Saibhre and Highway Sixty One are those most likely to genuinely secure prominent berths behind the leader. This race shape favours prominent racers who can travel close to the controlled pace and kick from a winning position, rather than closers dependent on a true-run test.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gallo Dell Cielo Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Gallo Dell Cielo sets an uncontested, honest pace and holds on under a confident front-running ride.
scenarios.body: Dictating from flag-fall on good turf over 2m with no pressure, the leader can conserve energy through the early stages and repel challengers who must come from off the pace against a steady tempo; the controlled fractions mean hold-up horses have no surge of pace to latch onto.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Bhean Saibhre or Highway Sixty One track the leader throughout and outstay Gallo Dell Cielo in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: With the pace modest, horses who are prominent from an early stage and travelling comfortably into the straight are ideally placed to wear down a front-runner who has done all the donkey work; Bhean Saibhre's course-distance profile and good-ground form make her particularly suited to this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or gaps open sufficiently in the straight for a true hold-up horse to weave through and finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: This shape requires the tempo to be deceptive enough to soften the leaders yet generate the kind of end-to-end energy that allows a late-running type to close; Bynx and Fine Print are the most credible candidates, though both are racing in a shape that does not suit their redistribution-adjusted roles.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the field bunches significantly at a false tempo and a lightly-weighted outsider produces an unexpected turn of foot in the straight.
scenarios.body: A scenario dependent on pace falling apart entirely and a horse landing a blow from an unfavoured position; Synchronize or Lariat could theoretically benefit from a muddling, stop-start gallop but this shape has low probability given Gallo Dell Cielo's tendency to control matters from the front.

watchPoints.text: Gallo Dell Cielo's 185-day absence is the single biggest race-shape disruptor — if fitness is lacking he may stop quickly in the straight, transforming a controlled race into a sprint finish that would hand the advantage to Bhean Saibhre and Highway Sixty One.

With six or seven genuine hold-up horses compressed into midfield, early crowding and traffic interference are likely between the 2m start and first bend at Tramore — watch for Bynx, Fire Coral, and Kings Gesture jostling for space in an unusually congested middle pack.

Stone Rulza carries top weight of 146lbs and is flagged as fading in the finish — if he hustles forward to avoid trouble and fades, he could impede hold-up horses trying to make progress in the closing stages.

Highway Sixty One's stamina at 2m is an open question having run exclusively at 12f throughout his recent form — Gary Carroll's judgement in the early stages, whether to hunt up prominently or drop slightly, will be a key shape-defining moment to observe at the start.

Gallo Dell Cielo's ground form is worth monitoring in running: all his wins came on standard/artificial surfaces rather than turf, so watch whether he travels as fluently as his front-running profile suggests on good turf — any signs of discomfort early could trigger a complete reshaping of the race.
